items.title: Pioneering AI hedge fund with returns of 1000% since inception discovers the downside of leverage
items.description: AI wunderkind Leopold Aschenbrenner has reportedly asked investors for an injection of fresh capital, and offered them to opportunity to buy some of its assets directly from the fund.

items.title: My friend and her husband own real estate. How can her children from a previous marriage get their fair share?
items.description: “Her husband is open to a trust, but he wants to be the administrator.”

items.title: ‘I feel lucky’: I’m 71 and inherited $20,000. What should I do with this money?
items.description: “I have an IRA, a high-yield savings account, four CDs and checking and savings accounts.”

items.title: Wall Street just suffered a historic crash in highflying stocks. Why a quick tech rebound could be a trap.
items.description: A bounce may be coming for those momentum stocks that have been brought back to earth, which could open up another selloff, says BTIG’s Jonathan Krinsky.

items.title: GDP grew so-so 1.5% in the second quarter, but don’t be fooled. The economy was much stronger than it looked.
items.description: The U.S. economy sped up in the spring even as the Iran war dragged on, boosted by the twin engines of consumer spending and business investment.

items.title: Fed-favored PCE inflation gauge falls for first time since pandemic, but danger far from over
items.description: The main inflation barometer used to set U.S. interest rates fell in June for the first time since the pandemic, underscoring why the Federal Reserve took no action this week to raise borrowing costs.

items.title: Congrats, Gen Z, you’re turning 30. Here are the most important money moves to make next.
items.description: Your parents may have shared advice that was fine when they were 30, but “the world has changed significantly” since then.

items.description: The CIO of Ranmore Funds isn’t too keen on U.S. valuations at present, but the beaten-down software sector is luring him back in.
